title: Six-rayed hexactinellid spicules reflect cubic, not closest, packing of vesicles

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Six-rayed hexactinellid spicules reflect cubic, not closest, packing of vesicles

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The six-rayed spicules of hexactinellid sponges form because the vesicles that mould them are arranged in linear series (cubic packing) rather than closest packing, so the spicules follow the angles and edges of a system of cubes instead of hexagons or dodecahedra.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the cells or vesicles by which they are conformed are not arranged in what is known as “closest packing,” but in linear series; so that in their arrangement, and by their mutual compression, we tend to get a pattern, not of hexagons, but of squares: or, looking to the solid, not of dodecahedra but of cubes or parallelopipeda.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Hexactinellid spicules and cubic packing”. Scope: hexactinellid (glass) sponges

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-11: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.49

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The packing mechanism makes a clear geometric prediction. Existing specimen data can show six-rayed geometry but are unlikely to contain the developmental vesicle arrangement required for a discriminating test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Reconstruct vesicle centers and nascent six-rayed spicules in developing hexactinellids, classify packing as cubic or close-packed, and test whether ray axes follow cubic nearest-neighbor directions. A close-packed arrangement with unchanged spicule geometry would refute the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mature skeletons cannot uniquely recover prior vesicle packing.

Developmental 3D data for glass sponges are exceptionally scarce.

fields.label: Dimension scores

data existence: 0.35

discriminating power: 0.7
analysis feasibility: 0.45

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Ray geometry is scorable from spicule images, but the claim is about the packing of the vesicles that moulded them. Public data are mostly cleaned spicules, not developmental histology, and they cover a modest fraction of hexactinellids in measurable 3D. Orthogonality is compatible with more than one mechanism, so a geometric pass would support only the form half of the claim.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure hexactinellid ray angles for cubic orthogonality versus the angles of closest packing, and, where tissue is preserved, score whether the vesicles around forming spicules are in linear cubic series. Orthogonal rays without cubic vesicle packing would leave the packing mechanism unshown.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Soft-tissue vesicle packing at the moment of spicule formation is rarely preserved or archived.

Orthogonal silica rays can also be produced by crystal habit, not only by cubic cell packing.

fields.value:

data existence: 0.4
discriminating power: 0.45
